name: cardiac — 4D volume rendering
desc: Volume rendering of a beating heart, reproducing the rendering options of two papers from the CHOP/SlicerHeart group (github.com/SlicerHeart/SlicerHeart) on public 3D Slicer sample data. Links to SlicerHeart and both papers are in the demo's footer. Opens on the 4D cine: ten cardiac phases from a 4D cardiac CT, playing at 10 fps with the CT-Coronary-Arteries-3 preset — and you can rotate WHILE it plays, because each phase is accumulated live rather than precomputed, so nothing stalls. Switch to the static 512×512×321 CTA and press “fly inside”: the CT-EndoVascular transfer function (transcribed verbatim from SlicerHeart and verified against a running Slicer) drops to zero opacity at 338 HU, so contrast-filled blood becomes invisible and the camera sits inside the chamber looking at endocardium — the JACC ventricular-septal-defect technique, with no segmentation step. Preset picker, ROI crop box with draggable handles, 4-up MPR with linked shift-move crosshair. Unlike VTK’s raycaster this jitters the ray and accumulates, so converged views have no banding: the contour rings visible in Slicer’s own render of the same data at the same camera are absent here.

name: endovascular flythrough
desc: Fly a camera through the inside of a contrast CT. The CT-EndoVascular transfer function (from SlicerHeart, verified byte-for-byte against a running Slicer 5.12) drops to zero opacity at 338 HU, so contrast-filled blood becomes invisible and the camera can travel down the aorta, into side branches and on into the chambers — looking at endocardium directly, with no segmentation and no precomputed centreline. SPACE toggles forward cruise, SHIFT+SPACE reverse, left-drag or the arrow keys look around, and SHIFT+click sets a target the autopilot steers toward, or reports how close the blood pool actually allows. Collision “rails” keep you inside the lumen: every frame the renderer casts a ray along the direction of travel and clamps the step to the distance to the wall — the same 50%-opacity GPU trace the crosshair pick uses. The MPR slices scroll to follow the camera, with the crosshair marking where you are. Streams the 512×512×321 CTA from a public JS2 bucket.

name: IHE Basic Image Review
desc: The IHE Radiology Basic Image Review (BIR) profile as a browser reader, on an arbitrary KiTS kidney-tumour CT streamed straight from the NCI Imaging Data Commons (c4kc_kits, dcmjs-parsed in a worker). The toolbar is the profile's exact tool set (Rev 1.3 §4.16.4.2.2.5.13) with its suggested icons and keyboard shortcuts — patient/study/series navigation, Scroll/Window/Zoom/Pan as mutually-exclusive modal tools, CT window presets (soft-tissue/lung/bone/brain), distance and Cobb-angle measurements, cross-hair, localizer lines, cine, annotation cycling, invert, and hanging-protocol layouts. The 4-up is Slicer-faithful — axial top-left with the coronal directly below it (shared L–R axis) and the sagittal beside the coronal (shared S–I axis) — plus a 3D volume render. The SlicerLive badge popup adds the controls that go BEYOND the profile: 3D volume-rendering opacity and per-segment segmentation display. Same reader component the SlicerRad radiology workspace runs; open ?series=<crdc-uuid>&bucket=<b> to review any IDC series.

name: colorize volume — 86 structures
desc: Slicer's Colorize Volume, in WebGPU: a chest/abdomen CT tinted by 86 TotalSegmentator structures — every rib and vertebra individually, five lung lobes, the heart chambers, the great vessels and the abdominal organs. The RGBA is composed per ray sample in the shader rather than baked into a texture, so every segment's opacity stays a live uniform: the SlicerLive badge opens grouped sliders (organs, heart, vessels, lungs, intestines, vertebrae, ribs, other bone, muscle) that fade a whole system in and out of a 55-million-voxel volume by rewriting a 1 kB palette. The same palette colours the segmentation overlaid on the CT in the three MPR slices, so one slider moves all four views together. A combobox picks any of twelve CT transfer functions transcribed from Slicer's presets.xml, which draw the unlabelled body and modulate each segment's brightness; the crop box and ROI are Slicer's own two switches. The label volume compresses to under a megabyte and loads first, so the segmentation is on screen as surfaces in under a second while the 61 MB CT streams in behind it from a public JS2 bucket. Data: NLST case 218750 from the NCI Imaging Data Commons (509×365×299 at 0.57×0.57×1.25 mm) with the CC BY 4.0 TotalSegmentator segmentations (doi 10.5281/zenodo.8347011).

name: codec race
desc: LiveCodec neural codec vs HTJ2K, racing on real IDC CT scans: two linked 4-up rows stream the same scan progressively to lossless, with per-row progress bars, simulated network speeds, and measured-bandwidth fairness reporting. Neural: 99 KB whole-volume preview decoded by hand-written WebGPU compute kernels.

name: SPINEPS vs IDC reference — spine review
desc: Vertebra-by-vertebra comparison of SPINEPS against IDC reference segmentations for 121 cancer patients (55 spine-mets with expert labels, 66 myeloma with nnU-Net labels). Parallel-coordinates chart of per-level 1−Dice; click a case to open the interactive SlicerLive comparison: SPINEPS and reference rows with linked MPR slicing + shared shift-move crosshair, per-method 3D shells with linked cameras, and a combined 3D view (method colours, tri-state opacity, extent control from one vertebra to the full spine). CT + masks stream as zarr from a public JS2 bucket; per-level Dice buttons jump every view to that bone.

name: nnLive — interactive segmentation (4-up)
desc: The payoff: a real CT in the SlicerLive 4-up where each click runs nnLive's FAITHFUL 192³ interactive segmentation (distilled nnInteractive: trunk encode + perclick decode, EDT-ball prompts, prev-mask feedback, auto-zoom) → mask → ColorizeVolume, live as a colored 3D volume + MPR overlay with a pushpin per click. Shift-click = background point. Coordinates correct end-to-end (RAS reslice + view→RAS→voxel). 188 MB weights stream from the public bucket.

name: SlicerLive — Live Segmentation Algorithms
desc: A WebGPU-native segment editor experiment: paint brush strokes and drop spheres, each a new coloured label, rendered as one crisp surface-model-style mesh. The pipeline is a GPU jump-flood signed-distance field (labelmap → colorized SDF) with a settle-refinement (near-exact Voronoi + pre-blended colour seams) — so a static segmentation renders smooth and cheap while orbiting, and neighbouring labels meet with a clean colour boundary. Paint is driven entirely by the mrson SegEdit op stream (no editing UI), interpolating pointer samples into continuous strokes in real time. Toggle SDF vs Gaussian render paths.

name: SlicerLive — Islands within islands (multi-material)
desc: A stress test for EMBEDDED / nested segmentations — tumors inside a liver, a necrotic core inside a tumor, touching cyst clusters, vessels threading an organ. Rendered through a single multi-material INTERFACE field: an unsigned distance to ANY label change, so every internal label↔label boundary surfaces (not just the outer segment↔background one) with its own colour and per-segment opacity — one field for arbitrarily nested layers, no per-segment SDF blow-up. Regenerate for new random scenarios; drop the Opacity slider to see the islands nested inside.

name: TotalSegmentator — 75 structures (WebGPU)
desc: A whole-body TotalSegmentator run (v1.5.6) on a National Lung Screening Trial chest CT, straight from the Imaging Data Commons — 75 structures rendered as ONE unified colorized signed-distance-field surface: every rib and vertebra its own crisp colored mesh, plus lungs, heart, liver and vessels, composited inside the CT volume render. The WebGPU successor to the legacy vtk.js TotalSegmentator viewer: a single field for all 75 segments (no per-surface slowdown), JFA-SDF + settle-refinement for surface-model geometry with pre-blended colour seams.

name: WebGPU real scene — MRHead (MPR + 3D VR)
desc: A REAL SlicerLive scene, live: the chunked OME-Zarr volume is streamed from the Jetstream2 bucket and gunzipped in your browser, then rendered by the TS/WebGPU backbone — 3 orthogonal MPR planes + a 3D volume render using the scene's own transfer function and true rotated IJK→RAS geometry. The direct replacement for the legacy vtk.js MRHead. Scroll a slice to scrub; drag 3D to orbit.

name: SlicerLive — SEGRoulette
desc: Spin a random segmentation out of 190k+ IDC DICOM SEGs (36 collections): the source CT/MR/PET and the DICOM SEG stream straight from the Imaging Data Commons buckets and are parsed in your browser (dcmjs), then rendered by the TS/WebGPU backbone — 3 MPR planes (grayscale + colored overlay) + a 3D view where the WHOLE segmentation is one unified colorized signed-distance-field surface (GPU jump-flood SDF + settle-refinement): crisp surface-model geometry, per-segment colour + opacity, colour seams pre-blended where labels meet — any number of segments in a single field. Hit Spin for another case.

name: LiveStory (prototype) — narrated MR head
desc: PROTOTYPE / placeholder. LiveStory (inspired by MinervaStory) turns a 3D Slicer scene into a narrated walkthrough — camera + slice views with captions and Wikipedia-style links on the left, the live SlicerLive WebGPU 4-up on the right; click a page to jump the view. Authored in Slicer via the LiveStory module and previewed straight from Slicer's own web server.

name: WebGPU: Landmark Deform (TPS)
desc: A port of the slicer-wgpu Landmark Deform selftest — a NONLINEAR thin-plate-spline transform applied during the ray march. DRAG a magenta target landmark to re-solve the spline and deform the volume live (GPU-local, no pipeline rebuild); the volume follows the pull. Cyan = source landmarks, magenta = draggable targets.

name: WebGPU: ROI Crop
desc: CTACardio cropped by an interactive ROI box. The box wireframe ray-marches in the SAME pass as the volume and drives the clip planes, so dragging a face/corner/centre handle re-crops the volume and moves the widget together — GPU-local, one uniform update, no pipeline rebuild. Grab-or-bubble: handles grab, empty space rotates the camera.

name: Selftest: Single Volume (CTACardio)
desc: SlicerWGPU Single Volume selftest, on the data it actually loads — CTACardio (512×512×321) streamed from the Jetstream2 bucket and ray-marched with the volume's own transfer function carried over from Slicer. Slicer-faithful camera bindings.

name: Selftest: Volume + Fiducials (CTACardio)
desc: SlicerWGPU Volume + Fiducials selftest — CTACardio with four markup lists of 25 control points, drawn as procedural SDF spheres composited inside the same ray-march so glyphs occlude and are occluded by anatomy.

name: Selftest: Multi-Volume (CTACardio + Panoramix)
desc: SlicerWGPU Multi-Volume selftest — CTACardio and CTAAbdomenPanoramix, each with its own transfer function, composited in one ray-march with Panoramix offset +200 mm along R exactly as the selftest places it.

name: Selftest: Segmentation (MRHead)
desc: SlicerWGPU Segmentation selftest — two segments thresholded straight out of MRHead intensities (Brain 40<v<120, High v>120), baked through ColorizeVolume and ray-marched: the native replacement for surface models.

name: TotalSegmentator-CT
desc: NLST chest CT with 73 TotalSegmentator organ & bone segmentations (IDC) — 3D surfaces + colored MPR overlays

name: IDC: TotalSegmentator
desc: Streamed LIVE from the NCI IDC AWS bucket + parsed in your browser with dcmjs — NLST chest CT + 73 TotalSegmentator organ/bone segments. No server, no pre-processing (~150 MB, give it a moment).

name: MRHead
desc: MR head — volume rendering + 4-up (axial / sagittal / coronal)

name: SEGRoulette (vtk.js)
desc: The original vtk.js SEGRoulette — spin a random IDC DICOM SEG + its source series, loaded client-side and rendered with surface models + MPR overlays. Superseded by the WebGPU SlicerLive SEGRoulette above.

name: ReMINDer — brain-tumour resection timeline
desc: The IDC ReMIND collection (Brain Resection Multimodal Imaging Database, 114 patients) at a glance, then one operation at a time. Dashboard: the five-stage surgical timeline with per-stage case coverage, a per-case coverage grid over stages and segmented structures, sequence and structure histograms — all from collection metadata, no pixels. Click a case for the timeline viewer: one row per acquisition in surgical order (pre-op MRI → iUS before dura opening → iUS after dura opening → iUS before intra-op MRI → intra-op MRI) × selectable axial/sagittal/coronal/3D columns, with tumour, cerebrum and ventricle segmentations. Every row is a different grid — a 1 mm MR of the whole head above a 0.125 mm oblique ultrasound block — so the views link in PATIENT SPACE: scroll or zoom and every row follows to the same RAS plane and the same millimetres, the 3D camera dollying with them, which is what makes intra-operative brain shift legible. CompareVolumes rock/fade/toggle between any two loaded volumes, and a per-row transfer-function editor (histogram + draggable opacity curve + window/level) for the volume renderings. DICOM streams straight from IDC's public bucket and is reconstructed in the browser (including the multi-frame 3D ultrasound) — and NOTHING is downloaded until you ask for it, one series at a time, each labelled with what it costs.
